methodology.operation: one ProbeBusiness.create in an interactive transaction, with or without awaited AuditService.log(input, tx)
methodology.latencyTimer: performance.now; includes transaction acquisition/begin/commit, log-call input construction and audit policy, redaction, JSON serialization and INSERT; excludes fixture record/metadata preparation, AuditContext setup, verification, DDL and cleanup
methodology.throughputTimer: closed-loop worker batch wall time; includes worker scheduling and actor-context setup, excludes warmup and verification
methodology.order: repeat/payload/concurrency, with mode-pair order AB, BA, BA, AB in a repeating four-repeat block
methodology.isolation: one fresh runner-owned database per invocation, one pool, unique business markers and audit table
methodology.comparison: manual-audit minus transaction baseline for the same payload, concurrency and repeat; baseline has the same business write and transaction but does not serialize or store audit metadata
limits: Closed-loop throughput at fixed worker concurrency is not a maximum-capacity or production SLA measurement.
Large metadata is 65536 UTF-16 code units including JSON syntax: 131072 bytes in NVARCHAR storage, not 64 KiB.
Scenario order, growing audit table, shared hosted-runner resources, cache state, and database/log growth can affect results.
Four-repeat ABBA mode ordering balances pair position but does not eliminate host noise or establish statistical significance.
P99 at the default 500 samples depends on about five tail observations; preserve every repeat and raw sample.
Only create transactions are measured; update/delete, network-distance, long transactions, schema changes and production read/index workloads are not represented.
Successful status means correctness checks passed; there is no universal latency or throughput pass threshold.
